newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL - EXTRAS SEEN BOOSTING UPM H1 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: POLL - EXTRAS SEEN BOOSTING UPM H1 PROFIT.

text.p: A Reuters survey of analysts covering Finnish equities showed a 3.38 billion markka median forecast for forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy's first half 1997 profit before extraordinary items and tax:
Their forecasts include a 1.5 billion markka one-off extraordinary gain from UPM's sale of Nokia shares. UPM has said it will book the 1.5 billion markka gain as operating profit.
Other extraordinary gains and costs are expected to have a roughly neutral effect on earnings, analysts said.
UPM-Kymmene's results are due on August 14 at 0800/0500 GMT.
In January-June 1996, UPM-Kymmene had a proforma 2,076 million markka profit before extraordinary items and tax.
In Q1, the group posted a 1,345 million markka profit before extraordinary items and tax.
In the Q1 report, UPM-Kymmene said it expected 1997 earnings to be at about the same level as in 1996.
The median of 12 analysts' forecasts for UPM's full-year 1997 profit before extraordinary items and tax was 5.07 billion markka (mean 5.16 billion) in a 4,180-6,900 million range.
UPM-Kymmene's full-year 1996 profit was 3.56 billion markka.

Contributors to the survey were Alfred Berg, AG Private Bankers, Aktia Bank, Aros Securities, Carnegie Securities, Den Danske Bank, Deutschen Morgan Grenfell, Enskilda Securities, Evli Securities, FIM Securities, Goldman Sachs, Handelsbanken, Interbank, Kleinwort Benson, Merita Securities and Opstock.
